Chloe / Marissa —

I reviewed Laura's redline and Chloe's notes. Below are suggested legal-safe defaults we can propose to GreenScale (keeping drafting concise):

1) Packaging conversion definition (proposed text snippet):
"‘Packaging Conversion’ means the event where a Customer's consumption of Model Units, as mapped in the MAP_worksheet, results in promotion of an SKU from 'pay-as-you-go' to 'packaged' status for the purposes of this Agreement. Events shall be deterministically computed based on timestamps and SKU mappings in the MAP_worksheet and shall not be subject to retroactive adjustment except as provided in Section 5 (Reconciliation)."

2) Soft cap / proportional taper (proposed text snippet):
"If, in any Billing Period, credits calculated under Section 2 exceed thirty percent (30%) of the Customer's recognized packaged spend for that Billing Period, Redwood shall apply a proportional taper equal to (Credits - 30% * Recognized Packaged Spend) * (90-day rolling average Recognized Packaged Spend / Recognized Packaged Spend for the Billing Period), provided that any amount deferred under the taper will be subject to a single quarterly reconciliation and may be netted against future charges within the next four (4) Billing Periods."

3) Clawback / reconciliation mechanics:
- Single reconciliation per quarter (no more than one adjustment per quarter).
- Ops must provide supporting event logs within 60 days of request.

Operational notes: the formula above keeps us within predictable exposure while giving GreenScale an ability to surface credits. Marissa, can you confirm whether our billing system can produce the 90-day rolling average and the per-period recognized packaged spend on demand (for audit)?

If ops says yes, I can prepare a clean redline. If not, we'll present a fall‑back simpler cap (e.g., absolute monthly cap of $X).
